title: questions/<qid>/configs.json — what S3.0 kept, and what it refused to decide (4.5.3)
description: Not a card: the screen's own record. Derived from what microscope_agent/src/screening.py already writes, not invented beside it. Until this existed the file carried neither `card` nor `artifact`, so the collector skipped it and the stage that decides how much compute a question costs left a record nobody checked. It also drops the `unvalidated` note that file carries: the note says no schema is registered, and this is that schema. Two invariants are the reason this is a schema and not a description -- an unresolved cap must not emit a fan-out, and a cap resolved by a person's preference must say that a preference is not evidence. Both were live defects before they were rules.

goal_id.description: the goal card this screen read. Without it the record cannot say which question it answered

goal_revision.description: and which revision of it. Re-running the screen after the goal changed produced a byte-identical record, because nothing inside named the revision -- so a fan-out issued against r2 and a card now at r3 are indistinguishable in the artefact. The ledger rule is (card_id, revision, hash); this is the same rule applied one layer down. Optional for one step only: making it required today would fail a configs.json already committed in the execution seat's path, and check 35 forbids one commit from spanning both boundaries, so the producer fills it first and this tightens after.

observable.description: an id in contracts/observables.json. A name outside the vocabulary never reaches this record -- the screen refuses first (4.5)

kb_version.description: pinned here for the whole fan-out, so siblings read one store (4.3.1). null means no store was reachable, and `degraded` then says so

composed_with.description: perturbation configurations this one rides with. A trap puts no light on a detector, so an observable needing one is produced by the imaging configuration it is composed onto (4.5.3)

rejected.description: kept rather than dropped: a configuration that was never a candidate and one that was refused are different facts, and only the second leaves a reason (P1)

excluded_by_person.description: configurations the goal's declared_exclusions took out of scope before screening, copied with the person's reason. NOT `rejected`, and the split is the point: `rejected` is a finding about what the instrument cannot do for this observable, and an exclusion is the person's decision about this goal, which says nothing about merits. Flattening them would make a later reader, or M5, count the person's choices as the screen's refusals. An excluded configuration is never screened, never counts against the cap, and gets no caller_id (decided 2026-09-24, plan.md at cbfa1ae). Optional: absent means the goal declared none

cap_resolved_by.description: how the cap was met. The outcome looks the same either way -- one configuration, a fan-out, a plan -- and they are not the same event. Flattening both into `resolved` makes 'how often could the screen not discriminate on its own' unrecoverable (M5)

preference_honoured.description: the configuration a person's tie-break selected, read only when the cap was unresolved (4.5.1 c)

preference_refused.description: preference entries that named something the screen had rejected, or that the table does not hold. A preference never overrides a capability refusal, and screening stops at the entry rather than sliding to the next

priority_terms_not_evaluable_here.description: goal priorities that need numbers S3 produces, and so cannot cut the list that decides whether S3 runs (4.5.3)

fan_out.description: one sub-agent per (candidate, axis). The ids are issued here because a sub-agent that chose its own could impersonate a sibling's (4.3.1 rule 3)

then.description: An unresolved cap emits nothing. The defect this prevents already happened: a discriminator was counted as usable without cutting, the cap read as resolved, and the fan-out went out over the sub-agent ceiling.

A human tie-break settles which capable configuration to spend the fan-out on and justifies nothing in the plan. The record has to carry that sentence, because the next reader sees only one configuration and a plan.
